chapter: Heroes, heard bands and Lunceford's life on the road
title: Count Basie and the nickname Steel Chest
summary: Crawford describes Basie mobbed by autograph seekers and calling him Steel Chest.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: And Louis Armstrong, yeah, when he'd get off that bandstand, well, when a man that big, everybody crowding him, want his autograph. What is an autograph? Nothing. Like Count Basie, I went up to hear him and Sy Oliver last -- yeah, last year. And so my wife went up and got Count, asked him to come down when he had intermission. And -- Jimmy -- Jimmy Crawford is over there at the table, right on the ringside.
Count Basie fought himself through that crowd and those heathen women, they wanted him to sign anything they

brought to him, just put your name on it. And he was trying to evade them, even toilet tissue, anything, napkins, anything. Count said, no, I don't sign no toilet tissues and no napkins. Well, that's taking advantage of a man. Want to rest and take it easy during his intermission, and those women were playing on him and pulling on him, trying to stop him.
But he came over to the table, and he -- naturally, he used to call me Steel -- Steel Chest.

Well, I can't tell you that. You know, he was like Lester Young, who had a name for everybody. Lester gave Sweets Edison, called him Sweets because he played that sweet trumpet. He had a name for everybody, Lester.
But now, you -- what's Steel Chest now?
Well, this Steel Chest, I don't know why he called me that. He -- we had names for one another.
